Stryker seeks mako Product Specialist to Enhance Surgical Precision in Seoul & GyeongGi Published: October 26, 2023
Stryker, a global leader in medical technologies, is actively seeking an Associate Mako Product Specialist to be based in the seoul and GyeongGi regions of South Korea. this critical role will focus on providing comprehensive clinical product support for stryker’s advanced Mako SmartRobotics system. The successful candidate will play a vital part in ensuring the optimal use of this cutting-edge technology, directly influencing patient and healthcare outcomes. The position includes a total rewards package, featuring bonuses, healthcare, insurance benefits, retirement programs, wellness programs, and service and performance awards, along with social and recreational activities specific to the location.
Key Responsibilities of the Mako Product Specialist The Mako Product Specialist position is a multifaceted role, demanding a combination of technical expertise, clinical understanding, and strong interpersonal skills.The primary responsibility involves delivering clinical and technical support to surgeons and operating room staff during procedures that utilize the Mako SmartRobotics system.This includes in-depth training on the robotic arm applications, associated equipment, and instruments to ensure ideal placement and precision during surgical interventions.
A crucial aspect of the role is the utilization of proprietary software to prepare pre-operative CT scans. this preparation is essential for the Mako SmartRobotics system, assisting surgeons in preoperative implant planning, implant sizing, and precise positioning.The specialist acts as a vital link between the technology and the surgical team, ensuring seamless integration and optimal performance. This pre-operative planning is a cornerstone of the Mako system, allowing for a tailored surgical approach based on the individual patient’s anatomy.
Beyond direct surgical support, the mako Product Specialist is responsible for meticulous reporting. This includes providing detailed reports and associated metrics to management, direct supervisors, and Stryker’s Quality/Regulatory representatives. These reports encompass case reviews, service feedback, customer complaints, and recommendations for improvements, contributing to the ongoing refinement and enhancement of the Mako system. Moreover, the specialist maintains and controls local Mako consigned inventory, ensuring its availability and proper management. Accurate inventory management is critical to ensuring that the necessary tools and equipment are available when needed, minimizing delays and maximizing efficiency in the operating room.
The role also extends to supporting sales and marketing activities. The Mako Product Specialist processes sales orders and provides forecast input to sales and operations teams. They also provide potential customers with hands-on demonstrations and explanations of the mako system, showcasing its capabilities and benefits. This involves actively selling the clinical advantages of the products and cultivating strong,positive relationships with key surgeons and OR staff at targeted accounts. Building these relationships is essential for fostering trust and encouraging adoption of the Mako system within the medical community.
Adherence to stryker’s quality system is paramount. The Mako Product Specialist is responsible for providing prompt and accurate complaint reports, ensuring that any issues are addressed swiftly and effectively. They also provide case coverage as needed, demonstrating adaptability and commitment to supporting the surgical team. This commitment to quality and responsiveness is a key component of Stryker’s overall approach to patient care and product excellence.
Qualifications and Attributes Candidates for the Mako Product Specialist position should ideally possess a minimum of one year of prior experiance in a sales and/or technical capacity within the medical, pharmaceutical, or healthcare industry. A strong understanding of the operating room surroundings is essential, along with a demonstrated knowledge of customer service principles and processes.
Key personal attributes for the role include strong problem-solving skills and the ability to thrive in a team-oriented environment. Excellent interpersonal and dialog skills are crucial for effective collaboration with surgeons,OR staff,and internal teams. The ideal candidate will demonstrate command, be willing to take control of situations, and possess the ability to analyze and comprehend written specifications, assisting customers with product selections that comply with those specifications.These attributes are essential for navigating the complex and demanding environment of the operating room and for effectively communicating the benefits of the Mako system to potential users.
Stryker’s Commitment to Healthcare Innovation Stryker’s dedication to improving healthcare outcomes is evident in its innovative products and services across MedSurg, Neurotechnology, Orthopaedics, and Spine. The company impacts more than 150 million patients annually, working alongside its customers around the world to advance medical technology and patient care. This commitment to innovation is a driving force behind Stryker’s success and its ability to deliver cutting-edge solutions to the healthcare industry.
Conclusion The Associate Mako Product Specialist position at Stryker offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the advancement of surgical precision and patient care in the Seoul and GyeongGi regions of Korea. By providing clinical and technical expertise on the Mako SmartRobotics system, the successful candidate will play a vital role in shaping the future of healthcare. Those interested in joining a dynamic and innovative company are encouraged to apply.
Apply Now
robotic Surgery’s Future: An Exclusive Interview on Stryker’s Mako SmartRobotics System Is robotic surgery poised to revolutionize healthcare, or is it just another technological fad?
To explore this question, we spoke with Dr. Anya Sharma,a leading expert in robotic-assisted surgery and medical technology innovation.
World-Today-News.com (WTN): Dr. Sharma, welcome. We’re excited to discuss Stryker’s recent recruitment drive for a Mako Product Specialist,highlighting the increasing importance of robotic surgical systems like the Mako smartrobotics system. Can you give our readers an overview of the importance of this technology and its role in modern surgical practices?
Dr. Sharma: “Thank you for having me. The Mako SmartRobotics system, and robotic surgery in general, represents a pivotal shift in surgical precision and patient outcomes.It’s not a fad; it’s a essential change in how we approach many surgical procedures. the core significance lies in its ability to improve accuracy,reduce invasiveness,and enhance recovery times for patients.Unlike customary surgery, Mako utilizes pre-operative planning through CT scan analysis to create a personalized surgical roadmap. This level of precision minimizes errors and allows for more customized procedures, something crucial for procedures like joint replacement.”
WTN: The job description highlights the specialist’s role in training surgeons and operating room staff on the system. How crucial is this specialized training, and what are the key aspects surgeons need to master?
Dr.Sharma: “The training is absolutely paramount. Surgeons aren’t simply transitioning from a scalpel to a joystick; they’re learning to interact with a complex system requiring a nuanced understanding of both its capabilities and its limitations. Key aspects of the training include:
Pre-operative Planning: “Mastering the use of the system’s software for 3D modeling and planning based on patient-specific CT scans. This includes accurate implant sizing, position planning and soft tissue assessment.” Intra-operative Control: “Surgeons need to become proficient in operating the robotic arms with dexterity and precision. This takes practice and ensures they maintain control throughout the procedure.” Troubleshooting: “Knowing how to handle unexpected scenarios, and understanding any limitations of the system, requires extensive theoretical and practical training.” WTN: Beyond surgical expertise, the role involves tasks like pre-operative CT scan planning, sales support, and meticulous reporting. How do these seemingly disparate responsibilities contribute to the overall success of the Mako system?
Dr. Sharma: “These different facets are intertwined. Effective pre-operative CT scan preparation directly impacts the accuracy of the surgical plan.Sales support expands the reach of the technology, bringing its benefits to more patients. And robust reporting ensures ongoing performance monitoring, process betterment, and compliance—all essential for the system’s long-term success and regulatory compliance. The role integrates technical, clinical, and commercial aspects, making it a pivotal one in the broader ecosystem of robotic-assisted surgery.”
WTN: The article emphasizes the importance of strong problem-solving skills and interpersonal abilities for the Mako Product specialist. Why are these soft skills as crucial as the technical skills?
Dr. Sharma: “In the operating room surroundings, things can and do go wrong. A skilled specialist can quickly adapt to unexpected issues and provide effective support to surgical teams under pressure.Further,surgeons,operating room staff,and management require excellent communication for knowledge transfer,problem-solving and feedback to drive continuous improvement. It’s a highly collaborative environment, demanding effective teamwork, adaptability, and strong communication protocols.”
WTN: What are the broader implications of expanding access to technologies like the Mako SmartRobotics system in regions like Seoul and GyeongGi?
Dr. Sharma: “Expansion into markets like Seoul and GyeongGi signifies a crucial step toward democratizing access to advanced surgical care. it means improved surgical outcomes and shorter recovery times for patients in these regions. This is notably significant given Korea’s advanced healthcare system: adoption of such superior surgical tools translates to a higher standard of care offered more widely within the population.The potential for improved healthcare infrastructure, and global dissemination of best surgical practices, is considerable.”
WTN: What advice would you give to someone considering applying for this role?
Dr.Sharma: “If you’re considering applying, you should possess a strong foundation in medical technology, coupled with excellent interpersonal and problem-solving skills. A background in sales or healthcare is a plus, but your passion for advanced surgical techniques and a commitment to improving patient outcomes should be your primary motivators. Demonstrated ability to learn quickly and adapt to new situations are also key.”
WTN: Thank you, Dr. Sharma, for your insightful perspectives. This has been a truly enlightening discussion.
Closing: Dr. Sharma’s insights underscore the groundbreaking nature of robotic surgery and the crucial role of skilled specialists like the Mako Product specialist. What are your thoughts on the future of robotic surgery and its potential to revolutionize the healthcare landscape? Robotic Surgery’s Dawn: A Conversation on Stryker’s Mako SmartRobotics System and the Future of Precision Surgery Is robotic surgery merely a technological advancement, or is it poised to redefine the very fabric of surgical practice? The answer, as we’ll explore in this exclusive interview, is far more profound then a simple yes or no.
World-Today-News.com (WTN): Dr. Evelyn Reed, a globally recognized expert in minimally invasive surgical techniques and robotic-assisted surgery, welcome. The recent Stryker recruitment drive for a Mako product Specialist highlights the growing importance of robotic surgical systems. Can you paint a picture for our readers of this technology’s transformative influence on modern surgical practices?
Dr. Reed: Thank you for having me. The Mako SmartRobotics system, and robotic surgery more broadly, isn’t just an incremental advancement; it’s a paradigm shift in surgical precision and patient care. The core importance lies in its ability to dramatically improve accuracy, minimize invasiveness, and significantly reduce patient recovery times. Unlike customary open surgery,Mako leverages advanced pre-operative planning,frequently enough incorporating detailed 3D modeling from CT scans,to design a personalized surgical roadmap. This level of customization minimizes errors and allows surgeons to tailor procedures more effectively to the individual patient’s anatomy—a critical advantage in complex procedures such as joint replacements, spinal surgeries, and orthopedic interventions.
WTN: The job description emphasizes the specialist’s role in educating surgeons and operating room staff. How essential is this specialized training,and what are the key skills surgeons must acquire to effectively utilize the Mako system?
Dr. Reed: This training is absolutely paramount. It’s not simply a matter of transitioning from a scalpel to a joystick; surgeons are mastering an intricate system requiring a deep understanding of its capabilities and limitations.The training must cover several key areas:
Pre-operative Planning: Surgeons need mastery of the system’s software for precise 3D modeling and planning. This includes accurate implant sizing, precise positioning, and thorough soft tissue assessment based on the patient’s unique CT scan data.
Intra-operative Control: Surgeons must develop dexterity and precision in controlling the robotic arms, ensuring consistent, controlled movements throughout the procedure. This requires significant practice and rigorous simulation.
* Troubleshooting and System Limitations: Thorough familiarity with potential system limitations and the ability to effectively troubleshoot unexpected events during a surgery is crucial.This demands both theoretical knowledge and considerable hands-on experiance within the operating room.
WTN: The Mako Product Specialist role encompasses responsibilities beyond direct surgical support, including pre-operative planning, sales support, and meticulous reporting. How do these seemingly disparate tasks contribute to the overall success of the Mako system?
Dr.Reed: These roles are intricately interconnected. Effective pre-operative CT scan planning directly impacts the accuracy and efficiency of the surgical plan, reducing operative time and improving outcomes. Sales support expands the system’s reach, increasing access to this advanced surgical technology for more patients requiring precise, minimally invasive procedures. robust reporting—including case reviews, feedback analysis, and complaint management—ensures ongoing performance monitoring, quality control, continuous improvement, and regulatory compliance. It’s a holistic approach uniting technical expertise with commercial acumen to ensure the long-term success and widespread adoption of the system.
WTN: The article stresses the importance of strong problem-solving skills and excellent interpersonal abilities for the Mako product Specialist. Why are these “soft skills” as crucial as technical proficiency?
Dr. Reed: In the high-pressure environment of the operating room,unforeseen challenges are unavoidable. A highly skilled specialist must quickly adapt to unexpected situations and provide unwavering support to the surgical team under stress. Furthermore,triumphant collaboration between surgeons,operating room staff,sales teams,and management demands exceptional interaction,active listening,and the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly and effectively– facilitating knowledge sharing and problem-solving. This collaborative environment necessitates superior teamwork skills and excellent communication protocols.
WTN: Expanding access to technologies like the Mako SmartRobotics system in regions like Seoul and GyeongGi carries significant implications. Can you elaborate on these broader impacts?
dr. Reed: The expansion into Seoul and GyeongGi represents a crucial step toward democratizing access to advanced surgical care. It means improved surgical outcomes, shorter patient recovery times, and reduced hospital stays—a significant benefit for patients and healthcare systems. This is particularly significant in regions with advanced healthcare infrastructure; the adoption of advanced surgical technologies like Mako elevates the overall standard of care across the board. The potential for enhanced healthcare infrastructure and fostering a global standard of excellence in minimally invasive procedures is considerable.
WTN: What advice would you offer someone considering applying for this role?
Dr. Reed: Candidates should have a strong foundation in medical technology, superb interpersonal skills, and a proven aptitude for problem-solving. Sales or healthcare experience is advantageous, but genuine enthusiasm for advanced surgical techniques and an unwavering commitment to improving patient outcomes should be paramount. The ability to adapt quickly to new environments and master complex systems is crucial in this dynamic field.
WTN: Thank you, Dr. Reed, for this insightful discussion. It’s been truly enlightening.
Closing: Dr. Reed’s insights highlight the transformative potential of robotic surgery and the crucial role of skilled specialists in ensuring its successful implementation. The Mako SmartRobotics system is not simply a technological advancement; it represents a significant step towards a future of more precise, less invasive, and ultimately more effective surgery.
